status: Definitions, metrics and primary comparisons fixed before computing the confirmatory tables. Not an external preregistration.
motivation: Instructor feedback (5 Nov 2026) asked for more tests to understand what makes the method work and fail at different levels.
disclosed_exploration: On 10 Nov 2026, quick checks of results/frame_features.csv showed that within-recording error falls strongly with fill progress, that prominence and model support rise with error within recordings, and that dropping the earliest 30% of frames gave lower Test I/II MAE than the Combined score.
The same session summarised visual_by_frame.csv by planned fill fraction (visual minus reference, model minus reference).
These observations motivated the experiments below; they are therefore post-hoc explanatory analyses, not independent confirmation.

data.frames: results/frame_features.csv regenerated by setup (portable numeric checks); 33 recordings; no new labels
data.unit: recording; group summaries average recordings equally

E1_error_levels.model: per recording, OLS e = b0 + b1*(q - mean(q)) + u; u split into slow = centred moving mean of u over 1.0 s (51 frames at 20 ms) and fast = u - slow
E1_error_levels.report: mean-square share of each level per recording (shares of mean(e^2); the OLS parts are orthogonal, the slow/fast cross term is reported), equal-recording group means, and RMS in cm
E1_error_levels.expectation_stated_before_computation: frame-level fluctuation is a minority of mean-square error in Test I and Test II

methods.combined: frozen development score, top fraction within each recording (original method)
methods.time_stratified_combined: split each recording into 10 equal-duration bins of q; keep the top fraction by frozen score within every bin (ceil per bin)
methods.no_selection: all frames (equals the expectation of random retention)

E2_what_acoustics_predicts.partial_correlation: per recording, Spearman correlation of each feature and the frozen score with |e| and with |fast|, with ranks linearly residualised on rank(q); median across recordings and count of negative signs
primary_comparisons: Test I: time_only vs combined, total target, 70%
Test II: time_only vs combined, total target, 70%
Test I: time_stratified_combined vs no_selection, frame_level target, 70%
Test II: time_stratified_combined vs no_selection, frame_level target, 70%
E2_what_acoustics_predicts.statistics: paired per-recording differences (8 recordings = 8 containers per group); exact two-sided sign-flip test over 256 assignments; 2,000 container bootstrap 95% intervals, seed 5305; Holm adjustment over the four primary comparisons
E2_what_acoustics_predicts.secondary: development-only ridge (penalty 0.1, equal recording weight) retargeted to log1p(|fast|), evaluated with time-stratified selection on the frame-level target

E3_reference_or_model.data: 46 author-confirmed visual water-band labels (experiments/results/visual_by_frame.csv), 6 Test I recordings; no new annotation

quantities.reference_gap: visual_fraction_midpoint - assumed_fraction (positive: water higher than the linear reference)
quantities.model_gap: audio_model_fraction - visual_fraction_midpoint (positive: model reports more water than visible)

E3_reference_or_model.report: per-recording phase means, then equal-recording means; count of labels whose reference or model value lies outside the visual uncertainty interval; descriptive only (6 recordings, provisional image-relative proxy)

E4_stft_window.features: same five features recomputed with python/reproduce_analysis.features; the score is refitted on development for each window with the same ridge settings
E4_stft_window.report: median partial Spearman of prominence, competition and refitted score with |fast| (controlling q); time-stratified 70% frame-level MAE change for Test I/II; Hann main-lobe width 2*fs/M
E4_stft_window.interpretation_rule: descriptive time-frequency trade-off; no window is selected using test results
